inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,504 normalized lines. The survey develops a continuous semantic arc from empirical prime-counting heuristics through analytic continuation, functional equations, Euler products and explicit formulas, then separates numerical RH work into evaluation, critical-zero location, and completeness certification before tracing applications to prime bounds, sign changes, Mertens, Goldbach, zeta-family transfer, pair correlation, and random-matrix heuristics. Formula extraction is often legible enough to identify mechanisms but exact symbolic reuse should be checked against the retained PDF.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and prime-counting introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Defines the prime-counting problem, develops Gauss's density heuristic and Li(x), and motivates explicit estimates and the RH error scale.

sections_inspected.label: Analytic foundations of zeta and RH
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Introduces zeta as a complex analytic object, analytic continuation, functional equation, xi, zero symmetries, RH, and the Euler-product bridge to primes.

sections_inspected.label: Prime-zero explicit formulas and error terms
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Compares prime-counting approximants, introduces weighted counts, explicit formulas, equivalent RH error criteria, zero-free regions, and probabilistic prime heuristics.

sections_inspected.label: Computational problem decomposition
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Recovers the approximate-functional-equation lineage and separates zeta evaluation, critical-zero location, and certification that no zeros were missed.

sections_inspected.label: Euler-Maclaurin, Gram test, and total zero counts
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Presents early evaluation and localization mechanisms, argument-principle counting, limitations of direct completeness tests, and partial critical-line results.

sections_inspected.label: Riemann-Siegel, Turing, Odlyzko-Schoenhage, and computational history
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Develops faster single- and multi-point evaluation, rigorous completeness certification, complexity comparisons, and provenance of large computations.

sections_inspected.label: Applications of certified zero computations
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Shows how computed zeros enable exact prime counts, explicit prime bounds, counterexamples to prime-counting and Mertens inequalities, and finite verification in Goldbach arguments.

sections_inspected.label: Complex analytic transfer, zeta families, pair correlation, and RMT
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Abstracts Riemann's analytic template, transfers it to L- and zeta-functions, studies zero-spacing statistics, and uses random matrices as a conjecture-generating dictionary.

sections_inspected.label: Warnings, reading guide, and acknowledgements
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the source's methodological warning about slow asymptotics and identifies only non-substantive navigation and acknowledgements thereafter.

sections_inspected.label: References and author metadata
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic provenance and contact metadata; inspected and excluded from semantic-unit selection.

accepted_units.title: From prime tables to a local density heuristic
accepted_units.why_material: Turns observed thinning and local irregularity of primes into the reusable move of modeling a discrete count by a local density and integrating that density, yielding Li(x) and the PNT scale.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the definition of pi(x), Gauss's probabilistic heuristic, Li(x), and its leading asymptotic.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The prose and conceptual transition are stable; the displayed sum and integral are legible but should be PDF-checked before exact formula reuse.

accepted_units.title: Why sharp prime-counting estimates make RH operational
accepted_units.why_material: Connects historical tabulation to explicit inequalities and explains that RH matters computationally because it controls the approximation error in replacing pi(x) by Li(x), not merely because it locates zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes examples of unconditional bounds and the stated RH-conditional error bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula-bearing text with degraded spacing and superscripts; the qualitative error-scale comparison is recoverable, while constants require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Complex analysis as the decisive representation change
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how replacing a real-variable counting problem by a complex analytic function changed what could be proved, while the later elementary PNT proof demonstrates that alternate representations can recover a theorem without reproducing the same insight.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes zeta's initial Dirichlet-series definition, Riemann's analytic shift, the maturation of complex methods, and the Selberg-Erdos elementary contrast.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Core prose is reliable; the zeta series and Selberg identity are formula-sensitive and should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Completion of zeta into a symmetric entire function
accepted_units.why_material: Combines analytic continuation, pole cancellation, Gamma factors, and Hadamard factorization into the reusable construction of a completed function whose zeros are exactly the nontrivial zeros and whose symmetry is manifest.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes two continuation routes, the functional equation, construction of xi, and its product over zeros.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several formulas have extraction damage; the prose establishes the construction, but exact normalizations and product factors require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Zero symmetries and the finite-height RH target
accepted_units.why_material: Derives the fourfold symmetry of nontrivial zeros from the functional equation and conjugation, then turns the global RH into the finite computational property 'RH up to height T'.
accepted_units.context_note: The transformation argument and terminology for critical zeros and finite-height verification are self-contained here.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The theta-series display is formula-dependent, but the zero-symmetry and finite-height definitions are clear in prose.

accepted_units.title: Euler products and explicit prime counts from zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Makes prime factorization analytic through the Euler product and then reverses the bridge with Riemann's explicit formula, representing prime counts as a smooth main term corrected by contributions from every nontrivial zero.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the Euler-product interpretation, the PNT zero-free-line criterion, R(x), Mobius inversion, and the computational series for R.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed products, sums, and exponents are central and partially degraded; conceptual use is safe from prose, exact formula use needs PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Weighted prime counts linearize the prime-zero bridge
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why theta, psi, and the von Mangoldt function are more natural analytic coordinates than pi(x): logarithmic differentiation of the Euler product turns multiplicative structure into a Dirichlet series and yields a simpler explicit formula, generalized by Weil through test functions and Fourier transform.
accepted_units.context_note: Definitions, logarithmic derivative, von Mangoldt explicit formula, and Weil's test-function flexibility are included.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula extraction is imperfect, especially summation indices; the semantic relation is prose-supported, but exact statements require the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Zero geometry controls prime-counting error
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how the largest real part of a zero determines attainable error exponents, giving RH-equivalent error estimates for psi and pi and interpreting improvements as enlargement of a zero-free region.
accepted_units.context_note: The span joins the explicit-formula heuristic to conditional and unconditional error terms and an explicit zero-free region.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exponent and region formulas contain OCR layout risk; qualitative implications are clear, while constants and powers should be PDF-verified.

accepted_units.title: Average von Mangoldt mass unifies PNT guises and predicts R(x)
accepted_units.why_material: Reframes primality density as the mean-value heuristic Lambda(n)≈1, derives equivalent PNT formulations, and uses prime-power weighting plus Mobius inversion to explain why R(x) is a better finite approximation than a bare integral.
accepted_units.context_note: Contains the three equivalent PNT forms and the heuristic passage from Pi(x) to R(x).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The displayed identities are readable at the level of structure; exact summation notation should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Three independent obligations in numerical RH verification
accepted_units.why_material: Separates computation of zeta to prescribed precision, localization of critical zeros, and proof that the localized list exhausts all zeros in the strip; this prevents numerical root finding from being mistaken for RH certification.
accepted_units.context_note: Historical recovery of the Riemann-Siegel formula supplies the transition into the three-part computational program.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose; table values and historical numerical magnitudes are not required for the conceptual decomposition.

accepted_units.title: Euler-Maclaurin evaluation with an explicit remainder budget
accepted_units.why_material: Provides an early exact expansion for zeta in which truncation parameters and a remainder estimate convert an infinite series into prescribed-precision computation, while exposing linear growth in cost with height.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Gram's failed elaborate route, the simpler expansion, the truncation rule, error estimate, and efficiency limit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Highly formula-dependent and visibly degraded in places; mechanism and cost statement are recoverable, but implementation requires checking the original PDF.

accepted_units.title: Hardy Z and Gram intervals turn complex zeros into sign changes
accepted_units.why_material: Changes representation from complex zeta values to a real-valued function on the critical line, so zero localization becomes sign-change detection; Gram points provide a structured grid while neighboring double-occupied intervals show the test is heuristic rather than infallible.
accepted_units.context_note: Definitions of Z, theta, Gram points, the sign-change argument, and Hutchinson's exceptions are present.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Exact phase formulas are OCR-sensitive; the real-valued reduction and sign logic are clearly supported by prose.

accepted_units.title: Counting all zeros is the completeness half of RH computation
accepted_units.why_material: Uses N(T), an argument-principle integral, and the theta-plus-S(T) formula to compare all strip zeros with found critical zeros, while identifying contour nonvanishing and unbounded S(T) as obstructions to the early method.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes Gram's moment-style completeness check, von Mangoldt's zero-count asymptotic, Backlund's formula, and the reasons it was superseded.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several displayed formulas are extraction-damaged; the certification logic and obstructions are explicit in prose, but exact contours and constants need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Simplicity assumptions and partial critical-line theorems
accepted_units.why_material: Records that a direct numerical scheme can fail in the presence of multiple zeros and distinguishes statistical evidence for simplicity from rigorous lower bounds on the fraction of zeros known to lie on the critical line.
accepted_units.context_note: Links the computational limitation to pair-correlation intuition and summarizes the progression from infinitely many to positive proportions.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose-dominant; numerical constants for the proportions are legible and should be source-checked if used quantitatively.

accepted_units.title: Riemann-Siegel: short oscillatory sum plus controlled remainder
accepted_units.why_material: Derives a fast critical-line evaluation by two treatments of a contour integral and a saddle-point expansion, reducing zeta evaluation to a short cosine sum plus a remainder whose rigorous bound enables finite-height RH checks.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the contour representation, transformation to Z(t), remainder expansion, and Titchmarsh's explicit bound.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: This is heavily formula-dependent and extraction has disrupted roots, floors, and coefficients; exact mathematical reuse requires scan/PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Turing's averaged discrepancy detects missed zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Replaces fragile pointwise control of the zero-count error by an averaged bound: if critical zeros were missed, the observed discrepancy would acquire a persistent offset contradicting the integral estimate, so searching only slightly beyond T certifies completeness below T.
accepted_units.context_note: The historical narrative motivates the method; the decisive mechanism is the comparison of N with the observed count through averaged S(t).
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The integral inequality is formula-sensitive but legible in structure; exact constants and hypotheses should be PDF-checked.

accepted_units.title: FFT amortization for many zeta evaluations
accepted_units.why_material: Transforms many evenly spaced exponential sums into rational-function evaluation at roots of unity and applies FFT, illustrating when a method with no single-point advantage becomes asymptotically superior for bulk zero verification.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the transformation, uniform interval of evaluation, precision guarantee, and comparison with Riemann-Siegel.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Displayed sums and complexity parameters are extraction-sensitive; the amortization mechanism is clear from prose.

accepted_units.title: Scale, reproducibility, and provenance of zero verifications
accepted_units.why_material: Traces the move from hand calculations to distributed and large-scale computation while explicitly noting that a major calculation was not repeated and that some results lacked journal publication, making provenance and reproducibility part of the evidence assessment.
accepted_units.context_note: The preceding table supplies historical scale; this span contains the substantive narrative and its caveats.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is stable; isolated numerical exponents should be checked against the PDF if used as exact records.

accepted_units.title: Exact pi(x) from an explicit formula and certified zeros
accepted_units.why_material: Contrasts direct prime enumeration with combinatorial and analytic methods, showing how a Riemann explicit formula plus tens of billions of high-precision critical zeros can yield an unconditional exact prime count.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the application framing, Meissel's reduced-data strategy, and Platt's zero-driven certification.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The conceptual comparison is prose-supported; exact record values and powers require PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Partial RH becomes a finite range of explicit prime bounds
accepted_units.why_material: Demonstrates how a verified finite-height zero statement is converted into explicit inequalities for prime-counting functions and gives a direct condition relating certified height T to the x-range of an RH-quality bound.
accepted_units.context_note: Combines historical bounds derived from verified zeros with Buthe's explicit partial-RH transfer.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Formula and constants are legible but exact quantitative reuse should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Initial numerical dominance can hide inevitable sign reversal
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that an inequality supported over enormous finite ranges can still fail infinitely often; high-precision zero data makes the reversal explicit, while logarithmic density captures the persistent but nonabsolute bias.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the explicit-formula decomposition, Littlewood's sign-change theorem, computational bounds, Lehman's certification condition, and logarithmic-density interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Several extreme exponents and the density formula are OCR-sensitive; the qualitative mechanism is clear, quantitative claims need PDF verification.

accepted_units.title: Mertens sums connect Mobius cancellation to RH and random-walk intuition
accepted_units.why_material: Represents reciprocal zeta through Mobius summation, obtains PNT- and RH-equivalent growth statements, and explains why a random-walk analogy actually warns that the seemingly natural square-root bound may be too strong.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes definitions of M and mu, the integral identity, equivalences, the random model, and the historical conjecture.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The integral and normalization of the random-walk law are formula-sensitive; the prose supports the semantic connection and heuristic warning.

accepted_units.title: Explicit zeros plus Diophantine alignment disprove Mertens
accepted_units.why_material: Decomposes a nonconstructive disproof into an explicit zero expansion, rigorous truncation control, verification of RH and zero simplicity to a finite height, and simultaneous phase alignment solved efficiently by LLL.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the prior stronger bound's failure, Odlyzko-te Riele inequalities, later explicit search, and the key finite computational pipeline.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The expansion terms and huge bounds contain extraction risk; the algorithmic stages are clearly recoverable from prose.

accepted_units.title: Formal analytic estimates plus finite L-function verification close Goldbach
accepted_units.why_material: Illustrates a hybrid proof architecture: theoretical major/minor-arc estimates handle the unbounded range while rigorous interval-arithmetic verification of many Dirichlet L-functions supplies the finite explicit component.
accepted_units.context_note: Distinguishes binary and ternary Goldbach and traces removal of a GRH dependency through stronger analysis and verified zero computations.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Prose is reliable; numerical bounds and height/modulus expressions should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: The Dirichlet-series reflex converts erratic arithmetic into contour geometry
accepted_units.why_material: Abstracts Riemann's method: encode an arithmetic function by a Dirichlet series, recover summatory behavior with Perron inversion, shift contours using analytic continuation, and if needed replace the function by a related one with a better analytic representation.
accepted_units.context_note: Definitions and the full encode-invert-shift-transfer workflow are contained in the span.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The Perron integral and Dirichlet series are formula-bearing; the workflow is explicit in prose, while exact analytic hypotheses require PDF checking.

accepted_units.title: Zeta-type structures transfer prime questions to new arithmetic settings
accepted_units.why_material: Explains why Euler products, functional equations, and zero hypotheses recur for Dirichlet L-functions and Dedekind zeta functions, transferring prime-distribution methods, finite computations, and bias phenomena to progressions and number fields.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes ERH/GRH terminology, equidistribution, Chebyshev bias, explicit computations, and the prime ideal theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Mostly prose; progression-count and asymptotic formulas are readable but should be PDF-checked for exact notation.

accepted_units.title: Selberg's structural checklist for a zeta function
accepted_units.why_material: Compresses a broad analogy into five interacting structural properties—Dirichlet series, coefficient growth, analytic continuation, functional equation, and Euler product—without treating any one surface form as sufficient.
accepted_units.context_note: The checklist is presented explicitly and follows examples that motivate it.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: List prose is stable; the compact displayed series and product need only routine PDF confirmation.

accepted_units.title: Rescaled zero spacings reveal pair correlation and repulsion
accepted_units.why_material: Moves beyond locating zeros to their relationships, normalizes changing density to unit mean spacing, formulates pair correlation, and connects a small near-zero density to repulsion and simplicity.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the N(T)-based rescaling, conjectural law, a rigorous smoothed consequence, and Odlyzko's numerical tests.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The rescaling and correlation integral are central and formula-sensitive; exact normalization should be checked against the PDF.

accepted_units.title: Random matrices generate moment conjectures but do not certify them
accepted_units.why_material: Builds a dictionary from zero statistics to Hermitian eigenvalues, uses matrix size near log T to predict all zeta moment constants, validates it against prior analysis and computation, and explicitly limits the inference because no general proof of the dictionary exists.
accepted_units.context_note: The span includes the physical origin, moment example, extracted pair-correlation figure and caption, Keating-Snaith prediction, function-field evidence, and the stated epistemic limit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: The page contains a plot whose extraction preserves only axes/caption and formulas with layout loss; conceptual claims are prose-supported, while the moment formula and graphical data require PDF/scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Slow iterated logarithms defeat finite numerical intuition
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies a concrete failure mode of computational conjecture formation: extremely slow unbounded growth can look bounded on every accessible range, so numerics require theoretical and heuristic support.
accepted_units.context_note: The Mertens conjecture is given as the source-specific cautionary example.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Pure prose with a simple iterated-log example; no material representation dependency.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Zeros as a bidirectional computational interface
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Euler products encode primes into zeta, while explicit formulas decode zero data into prime counts and bounds; the real parts and verified height of zeros determine the strength and range of the decoded information.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The survey states representative formulas and applications but does not supply full derivations or error analyses, and exact formula text has extraction risk.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Evaluation, localization, and completeness are distinct proof obligations
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: A rigorous finite-height RH computation must evaluate zeta accurately, locate critical zeros, and independently certify that none were missed; successive algorithms optimize different layers rather than solving a single undifferentiated task.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Complexity comparisons are survey-level and tied to the stated historical algorithms, not a current implementation benchmark.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Computation can expose false extrapolation from vast finite ranges
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The pi-versus-Li and Mertens episodes show that persistent finite numerical behavior is not a reliable asymptotic law; explicit formulas and phase-alignment methods can turn zero data into counterexamples, while slow growth explains why naive searches mislead.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The synthesis diagnoses a methodology of falsification, not a general theorem that every empirical inequality eventually fails.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Riemann's encode-invert-shift pattern transfers across arithmetic structures
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Arithmetic data are encoded by Dirichlet series or zeta-type functions, analytic continuation enables contour movement, Euler products preserve atomic structure, and finite zero verification can then feed explicit arithmetic results beyond the original zeta setting.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source provides a structural survey and examples, not sufficient hypotheses for applying the template to an arbitrary new function.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Statistical zero models generate testable mathematics without becoming proof
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Pair correlation and random-matrix analogies organize predictions about simplicity, repulsion, and moments and are checked against high-zero computations, but agreement remains conjectural evidence unless independently proved.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source does not justify the random-matrix dictionary in general and explicitly warns that it may fail outside tested regimes.

within_source_saturation: Saturated for source-grounded semantic depth: every mathematical section was inspected, and the accepted units cover each distinct mechanism, equivalence, computational certification layer, application, transfer pattern, statistical reframing, and source-specific warning. Unselected text consists predominantly of biographies, page furniture, illustrative tables, repeated historical records, reading guidance, acknowledgements, references, or a plot whose visual content is not fully recoverable from the normalized text.
stop_reason: The final substantive source-specific mechanism is the warning at lines 1287-1294 that iterated-log growth can look bounded numerically. Lines 1295-1504 contain reading guidance, acknowledgements, references, and author metadata, so further segmentation would repeat represented mechanisms or select non-semantic/bibliographic material rather than add mathematical depth.
